validity.recommendation: no action needed on existence/classification; existing entity is correctly identified and currently operating
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: strongly confirmed. TIGT is a real, currently-operating FERC-jurisdictional interstate natural gas transmission system, formerly Kinder Morgan Interstate Gas Transmission (KMIGT), acquired by Tallgrass Energy Partners from Kinder Morgan in 2012 (independently confirmed by NYT DealBook, Aug 20 2012, via archive.nytimes.com -- the sale also included Trailblazer Pipeline and a 50% REX stake for ~$1.8bn total, NOT a TIGT-only price). Tallgrass's audited 2016 Form 10-K (SEC/annualreports.com) describes 'the Tallgrass Interstate Gas Transmission system, a FERC-regulated natural gas transportation and storage system with approximately 4,655 miles of varying diameter transportation pipelines serving Wyoming, Colorado, Kansas, Missouri and Nebraska.' FERC's own eTariff system (etariff.ferc.gov, sid=189094) carries an active tariff record for 'Tallgrass Interstate Gas Transmission, LLC,' and a Feb 2023 FERC rate docket (RP23-492-000, via insightengine.org docket tracker) shows TIGT filing a negotiated-rate agreement -- current, active regulatory activity as of 2023, consistent with the sheet's LastUpdated=2023-08-25 and Status=operating. Tallgrass's current corporate site (tallgrass.com/energy-solutions/natural-gas, live 2026) still lists TIGT among the FERC-regulated systems it operates today, alongside REX, Ruby, Trailblazer, Cheyenne Connector and East Cheyenne Gas Storage. DUPLICATE CHECK: not a duplicate/relabel of any other roster row -- TIGT's footprint (WY-CO-KS-NE-MO) does not overlap Cheyenne Plains, Cheyenne Connector, CIG, WIC, TransColorado or any other batch-4 row; those are documented as distinct FERC-certificated systems in the same 10-K. CONTEXT (not a defect on this row): the 10-K also discloses that TIGT abandoned ~433 miles of mainline gas facilities in 2012-2014 (FERC Docket CP12-495, the 'Pony Express Abandonment'), converting that pipe to crude-oil service as the Pony Express Pipeline (a GOIT/oil asset, out of scope here) and building replacement gas facilities to keep serving remaining TIGT gas customers. The 4,655-mile figure I'm confirming below is the POST-conversion (current) system total, consistent across all sources checked. CAVEAT (attribution, low-severity): Owner1='Tallgrass Energy' [100%] is directionally correct as the current operating brand (matches TIGT's listing on tallgrass.com today), but in Jan 2019 Blackstone Infrastructure Partners agreed to acquire a controlling interest in Tallgrass Energy, LP (deal closed 2020, shareholder-approved per Hart Energy/Reuters/BusinessWire coverage of the April 2020 vote); Tallgrass has been a private, Blackstone-Infrastructure-Partners-led portfolio company since 2020, not the publicly-traded LP the 2012/2016 sources describe. 'Tallgrass Energy' alone doesn't surface that PE ownership layer -- same pattern as Kern River's 'Kern River Gas Transmission Co' masking Berkshire Hathaway Energy noted elsewhere in this batch. I could not find a source stating current(2023-2026) ownership percentages broken out by ultimate investor, so I'm not proposing a replacement value -- flagging for a researcher to pursue via a Tallgrass investor-relations fact sheet or S&P/Bloomberg ownership record if precision is wanted.

validity.recommendation: re-verify Capacity=830 MMcf/d; no independent source states this figure for TIGT alone
validity.researcher_notes: Capacity=830.00 MMcf/d could not be independently corroborated. As with StartYear1, GEM's own gem.wiki page lists 'Current capacity: 830 Million cubic feet per day' with NO citation number, unlike Owner/Length on the same page which cite footnote [3] (the 2016 annual report) -- the annual report does not contain an 830 MMcf/d figure. SEC full-text search (efts.sec.gov) across all Tallgrass entity filings returns ZERO hits for the phrase '830 MMcf' anywhere. Open-web search (DuckDuckGo, Bing) for 'Tallgrass Interstate Gas Transmission' + '830' surfaces only GEM's own wiki page and GEM-mirroring sites (wipi.ai.kr, sourcewatch.org) -- i.e. the figure appears to circulate ONLY via GEM-derived copies, not from an independent origin. What I DID find: Tallgrass's 2016 10-K states a COMBINED 'Approximate [Design] Capacity' of 2.0 Bcf/d (2,000 MMcf/d) for TIGT System + Trailblazer Pipeline together (5,109 mi combined = TIGT's 4,655 + Trailblazer's 454, confirming the table is the two systems summed); a 2014 8-K states a combined design capacity of 1,926 MMcf/d for the same two-system grouping. Netting out Trailblazer's own GEM-recorded capacity (878 MMcf/d, this same roster, P0266) against either combined figure implies TIGT alone would be roughly 1,050-1,120 MMcf/d, materially higher than 830 -- though this is an inference from combined totals, not a source that states TIGT's capacity directly, so I'm not proposing it as a replacement value. Flagging as a genuine spec concern rather than passing it silently: the 830 figure has no traceable independent origin I could find, and the circumstantial math points the other way.

Evidence is mixed, not clean enough to stage. The 2016 10-K states the company retains natural gas from shippers to cover 'electrical compression costs ... on the TIGT System' (implying at least some electric-driven compression), but a separate passage in the same filing refers generically to 'the natural gas used to run our natural gas compressor stations' across the whole family of systems (REX/TIGT/Trailblazer), and a FERC docket for REX (not TIGT) explicitly confirms 'both gas and electric powered compressor stations' on that system. I could not find a document that states TIGT's compressor fuel mix (gas-fired vs. electric-drive) cleanly and specifically. Rather than force a single-value guess between 'Natural Gas' and 'Electricity' for what may genuinely be a mixed fleet, leaving UNRESOLVED -- flagging the 'electrical compression costs...TIGT System' language as a lead for a follow-up pass.

cross_row_leads.facts: Tallgrass's 2016 10-K states Trailblazer Pipeline Company LLC owns 'the Trailblazer Pipeline system, a FERC-regulated natural gas pipeline system with approximately 454 miles of transportation pipelines, including laterals, that begins along the border of Wyoming and Colorado and extends to Beatrice, Nebraska.' GEM's roster shows P0266 at len=436.0 km/mi -- an 18-unit gap worth checking against this 454-mile figure (units: the 10-K states miles). NOTE: the batch brief's lead that 'Tallgrass pursued a conversion of Trailblazer out of gas service' may be conflating two different Tallgrass conversions -- the ONE conversion documented in this 10-K (FERC Docket CP12-495, 'Pony Express Abandonment,' 2012-2014) converted ~433 miles of TIGT (P0208, this row), not Trailblazer, into the crude-oil Pony Express Pipeline. Worth double-checking which system the status-review lead for P0266 actually refers to.

Same 10-K: Rockies Express east-to-west capacity was 2.6 Bcf/d as of the 2016 filing, inclusive of the Zone 3 Capacity Enhancement Project (FERC Docket CP15-102) that added an incremental 0.8 Bcf/d, completed/placed in service Jan 6, 2017 (pre-enhancement east-to-west capacity was therefore ~1.8 Bcf/d).

The Rockies Express Zone 3 Capacity Enhancement Project (the likely basis for P2517 Cheyenne Hub Enhancement, len=0) added 0.8 Bcf/d (800 MMcf/d) of east-to-west capacity per FERC Docket CP15-102, completed Jan 6, 2017 -- for comparison against P2517's recorded 1,000 MMcf/d if not already resolved by the batch-3 sibling-row work.
